architecture: independent repositories, composed contracts, no runtime package dependency

operations.output: cross-repo result envelope with explicit blockers and evidence refs

operations.required_authority: scoped HUMAN WORK command capability; ROS authority_ref is never sufficient alone
operations.output: WORK repository-issued result, evidence refs and release/package refs

immutable package identity and only exact final-package member bytes (which may contain private case content) under a separate native WORK tenant/case-scoped package-read capability; never raw credentials or original source-byte export

mapping.request: ROS operation envelope validated first; adapter maps only allowlisted operation/input fields into public WORK requests
mapping.scope: ROS case_id and privacy scope must map exactly to WORK tenant_id/case_id; mismatch blocks before execution
mapping.authority: opaque ROS authority_ref is resolved by a trusted host to a native WORK capability; it is not forwarded as authorization truth
mapping.concurrency: ROS expected_head is an orchestration precondition; WORK expected_case_sequence/CAS remains authoritative for domain writes
mapping.idempotency: adapter binds ROS idempotency key plus request digest to the exact WORK command ids/results; different digest blocks
mapping.evidence: existing cross-repo evidence/result/provenance envelopes carry references; original bytes remain in scoped WORK storage
mapping.result: native WORK result is authoritative; adapter derives a neutral result without rewriting the native record

gaps.description: PB02 is a builder candidate at the pinned WORK baseline and PB03 is the current builder candidate; candidate-SHA binding, CI and independent exact-SHA review remain required.
gaps.dependency: PB03 candidate-SHA binding, CI and independent exact-SHA review

gaps.description: No adapter maps ROS operation scope, authority, CAS and idempotency to public WORK boundaries.
ROS CIRP artifacts have no accepted mapping to exact WORK Ref revisions, HUMAN decisions and legal applicability pins.
gaps.dependency: supported type contract and independent legal/domain review

gaps.description: All three LW-PB-01 document types remain NOT SUPPORTED / FUTURE.
gaps.dependency: per-type schema, profile, fixtures and HUMAN legal/type admission

gaps.description: The observed ROS remote-tracking ref was not refreshed during this run by policy.
gaps.dependency: supervisor-provided fresh exact ROS SHA or later authorized fetch

invariants: unknown schema, operation, scope, authority, version or mapping blocks
ROS never writes WORK storage, ledger or release state directly
WORK never imports lukart_ros as a runtime package dependency
ROS orchestration success cannot manufacture WORK validation, HUMAN approval or FINAL
no caller-supplied PASS, legal applicability, render hash or release receipt becomes authoritative

raw credentials and original source bytes never cross the operation envelope; private case content crosses only as exact final-package member bytes returned by ros.work.generator.read-package.v1 after explicit native WORK tenant/case-scoped package-read authorization and HG-09; the operation remains blocked until its adapter and review gates are admitted
native records remain authoritative and neutral envelopes are derived views
replay requires exact code, contract, policy, input and artifact identities
unknown, NOT_RUN, skipped or missing evidence is never PASS
non_goals: sharing a database or Python package runtime
using the ROS renderer for WORK DOCX/PDF
automatic legal judgment or HUMAN gate substitution
external filing, delivery, signature or publication
declaring any LW-PB-01 document type supported
acceptance: contract structure and pins validate deterministically
unknown operation and scope mismatch fail before WORK invocation
authority_ref without a native WORK capability fails
same idempotency key with a different digest fails
neutral result preserves native WORK result identity and provenance
no runtime import or direct database dependency exists between repositories
positive execute/read-package tests remain prohibited until their blocking gaps close
